Source layout per `docs/conventions/authoring.md`: `src/components/<name>.ts` (+ paired `.css` for static records), `src/utilities/<name>.ts`, `src/rules/`, `src/declarations/`. The `COMPONENTS` registry lives in `src/components/index.ts` — no `card.ts` exists there, confirmed by absence in that file's imports.

**Class-prefix mechanics** (`src/lib/sentinel.ts`, `src/lib/helpers.ts:10`): source `.css` files author classes with a placeholder `.pfx-` (`SENTINEL`), swapped at build time for the real prefix. Default prefix is `instui` (`DEFAULT_PREFIX = "instui"`), so `.pfx-checkbox` → `.instui-checkbox`. `docs/conventions/authoring.md:19-25` documents the modifier convention: `.${p}<comp>.-<prop>-<val>` (e.g. `-color-secondary`, `-size-sm`), booleans as bare prop names (`-clickable`), sizes on one scale (`xs,sm,md,lg,xl`) with short+long aliases, and nested parts as unprefixed descendant classes (`.instui-tabs .tab`, not BEM `__`).

### 1. Card (with elevation)
There is **no dedicated `.instui-card` component**. InstUI/pantoken builds cards from the **View utility** — `formats/components/src/utilities/view.ts` (lines 10-152) — composed with the **elevation declaration** — `formats/components/src/declarations/elevation.ts` and `packages/utils/src/declarations.ts:19-42`.

- Classes: `.instui-view` + modifiers `-background-{primary,secondary,primary-inverse,brand,info,alert,success,danger,warning,transparent}`, `-border-radius-{small,medium,large,circle,pill}`, `-border-width-{small,medium,large}` + `-border-color-*`, `-shadow-{resting,above,topmost}`.
- Elevation tokens: `--instui-elevation-resting/above/topmost`, plus aliases `--instui-elevation-depth1-3`, and **card-specific aliases `--instui-elevation-card` (= resting) and `--instui-elevation-cardHover` (= topmost)** — `packages/utils/src/declarations.ts:27-32`. These are also exposed as standalone box-shadow utility classes `.instui-elevation-card` / `.instui-elevation-cardHover` (generated in `formats/components/scripts/generate.ts:107` via `tokenUtilitiesCss`, `packages/utils/src/index.ts:390-405`).
- Example markup (from `view.ts:148`): `<div class="instui-view -background-secondary -border-radius-medium -shadow-resting">A card-like surface.</div>`. For elevation on hover, swap `-shadow-resting` for `var(--instui-elevation-cardHover)` inline or add the `.instui-elevation-cardHover` utility on `:hover`.
- Card title/header text uses **heading variants**, not a card part: `.instui-heading -variant-title-card-mini/-card-regular/-card-section` (`formats/components/src/components/heading.ts:28-30,48-50`), plus `-border-bottom`/`-border-top` for a rule under a card header (line 61-67).

### 2. Tabs
File: `formats/components/src/components/tabs.ts` (thin wrapper) + `formats/components/src/components/tabs.css` (actual CSS/doc, 131 lines).
- Root: `.instui-tabs` (flex column). Parts: `.list` (row of tabs, `role="tablist"`), `.tab` (`role="tab"`), `.panel` (`role="tabpanel"`).
- Modifiers: `.tab.-selected` / `[aria-selected="true"]`, `.tab.-disabled` / `[aria-disabled="true"]`/`:disabled`, root `-overflow-scroll` (horizontal scrolling tab list, hides scrollbar), root `-variant-secondary` ("folder" tab style with rounded borders that visually merge into the panel).
- State can be driven by class OR ARIA attribute — CSS matches both (`tabs.css:74-77`).
- Tokens: `--instui-component-tabs-default-background`, `--instui-component-tabs-tab-{default,secondary}-{text-color,font-*,hover-border-color,selected-*}`, `--instui-component-tabs-panel-{border-width,border-color,background,text-color,font-*}`.

```html
<div class="instui-tabs">
  <div class="list" role="tablist" aria-label="Default tabs">
    <button class="tab -selected" role="tab" aria-selected="true">Overview</button>
    <button class="tab" role="tab" aria-selected="false">Details</button>

Two independent mechanisms both toggle `.dark` on `<html>`, and they must stay in sync:

- **pantoken's own theme system**, in `docs/.vitepress/theme/theme.ts`:
  - `applyTheme()` (theme.ts:106-113) sets `html.dataset.pantokenTheme = theme` (i.e., `data-pantoken-theme` attribute) and calls `syncSchemeClass()`.
  - `syncSchemeClass()` (theme.ts:88-100) removes the `.dark` class from `<html>` when a single-scheme theme (`canvas`/`canvasHighContrast`) is active, and restores the remembered light/dark choice when switching back to `rebrand` (the only scheme-aware theme, per `supportsScheme()` at theme.ts:48).
  - A blocking inline `<head>` script in `docs/.vitepress/config.ts:451-456` runs before first paint, reading the `pantoken-theme` localStorage key and stripping `.dark` for non-rebrand themes to avoid a flash.
  - `docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts:130-133` calls `applyTheme(getStoredTheme())` on `enhanceApp` to reconcile state client-side.
  - `ThemeSelector.vue` (`docs/.vitepress/theme/components/ThemeSelector.vue:24-28`) is the UI for picking the pantoken palette (rebrand/canvas/canvasHighContrast) — it calls `applyTheme(theme)` on selection. So the canonical light/dark signal is the `.dark` class on `<html>`, set by VitePress's appearance toggle and gated/cleared by pantoken's `syncSchemeClass`. The `data-pantoken-theme` attribute (also on `<html>`) selects the palette (rebrand vs. canvas vs. canvasHighContrast), a separate axis from light/dark.

## 2. How the generated component CSS keys dark-mode overrides

Searched `formats/css/generated/style.css`, `formats/css/dist/`, and `formats/components/generated/*.css` for `.dark`, `data-theme`, and `prefers-color-scheme` — **none of the pantoken-generated token/component CSS uses any of those selectors.** Instead it uses the native CSS `light-dark()` function, e.g. `formats/css/generated/style.css:2628`:

### 6. Fix broken InstUI icon rendering — `docs/scripts/cdn-icon-manifest.ts` + `IconPicker.vue`

Root cause confirmed: `docs/scripts/cdn-icon-manifest.ts:14-16`'s `extractPath()` —

```ts
function extractPath(svg: string): string {
  return /\sd="([^"]+)"/.exec(svg)?.[1] ?? "";
}
```

— runs a non-global regex against the icon's full SVG markup and returns only the *first* `d="..."`
match anywhere in the string (used at line 26: `path: extractPath(icon.svg)`). Lucide icons routinely
compose a base shape (`<circle>`, `<rect>`, a triangle `<path>`) plus separate detail `<path>`/`<line>`
elements (a stem, a dot); `extractPath` keeps only one of them and silently drops the rest, or returns
`""` when the first/only shape element has no `d` attribute at all (e.g. a bare `<rect>`). Confirmed
against the generated manifest: `info` keeps only the vertical stem (circle outline and dot lost),
`square` and `circle-alert` come out as `path: ""` (nothing renders — those are `<rect>`/`<circle>` +
`<line>`s with zero `<path>` elements), `triangle-alert` keeps only the outline (stem + dot lost) —
exactly the "renders as a bare circle/triangle/square" symptom reported. The upstream data is not at
fault: `packages/core/src/icons.ts`'s `lucideModuleToSvg()` already reconstructs the full multi-element
`<svg>` correctly; the loss happens only in this docs-local extraction step.

Fix:
- In `docs/scripts/cdn-icon-manifest.ts`, replace `extractPath()` with an `extractInnerMarkup(svg)` that
  captures everything between the outer `<svg ...>` and `</svg>` tags (e.g.
  `/<svg[^>]*>([\s\S]*)<\/svg>/.exec(svg)?.[1] ?? ""`), and change the manifest field from `path` to
  `markup` (rename at the write site, line 26, and in the emitted JSON shape). Leave the existing
  `viewBox` extraction alone — it's a single-attribute regex and not lossy.
- In `IconPicker.vue`: rename `InstUiEntry.path` → `InstUiEntry.markup` (interface at lines 6-11), and
  change the render (lines 252-259) from a single `<path :d="icon.path" />` to
  `<svg class="icon-picker__svg" :viewBox="icon.viewBox" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" v-html="icon.markup"></svg>`.
  This is a deliberate `v-html` use — flagged here rather than silently introduced — but it's safe: the
  markup is fully build-time-generated from vetted source (`lucide-react`'s shipped module source and
  pantoken's own `custom` icon set, both parsed in `packages/core/src/icons.ts`), baked into a static
  JSON asset at build time, never runtime or user-supplied input. It's also the only approach that's
  correct for both `lucide` and `custom` sources regardless of how many shape elements an icon uses,
  without hand-rolling an SVG element parser.
- Re-run whatever generates `cdn-icon-manifest-instui.json` (part of the `docs:assets` script per
  `docs/package.json`) so the fix takes effect, and re-check the four icons named above render fully.

<result>## Summary of findings

### 1. Location and size of the full generated `icons.css`

Built in two places, both containing all 1,829 icon rules (~1828 icons):

- `formats/components/generated/icons.css` — **247,039 bytes** (1,829 lines, pretty-printed with spaces)
- `formats/components/dist/icons.css` — **232,349 bytes** (1 line, minified)

Content is one CSS rule per icon:
```
.-icon-a-arrow-down, .-render-icon-a-arrow-down, .-render-custom-icon-a-arrow-down { --pantoken-glyph: var(--instui-icon-a-arrow-down); }
```
(`formats/components/generated/icons.css:2`)

Note: `icons.css` alone only maps class → `var(--instui-icon-<name>)`. The actual custom-property *values* (the mask data-URIs) live in a separate full token sheet — `formats/css/generated/style.css` (1,510,145 bytes) / `formats/css/dist/style.css` (1,477,583 bytes) — which defines all 1,830 `--instui-icon-*` properties. There's also a per-icon variant at `formats/components/generated/icons/<name>.css` that self-contains both the var definition and the glyph class (e.g. `formats/components/generated/icons/info.css`), built by `formats/components/scripts/build-icon-entries.ts` for "selective CDN delivery."

### 2. Value format — confirmed correct, full multi-shape SVG

Each `--instui-icon-<name>` is a `url('data:image/svg+xml;utf8,...')` value that encodes the **entire** SVG element tree, not a single extracted path. Verified by decoding:

- `info` (`formats/components/generated/icons/info.css:1`): `<circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"/><path d="M12 16v-4"/><path d="M12 8h.01"/>` — circle + 2 paths, all present.
- `square` (`.../icons/square.css:1`): `<rect width="18" height="18" x="3" y="3" rx="2"/>` — correct single rect.
- `circle-alert` (`.../icons/circle-alert.css`): `<circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"/><line x1="12" x2="12" y1="8" y2="12"/><line x1="12" x2="12.01" y1="16" y2="16"/>` — circle + 2 lines, all present.
- `triangle-alert` (`.../icons/triangle-alert.css:1`): 3 `<path>` elements combined correctly.

**This pipeline does not have the docs manifest's bug.** The bug is local to `docs/scripts/cdn-icon-manifest.ts:15`:
```ts
// Extract the first <path d="…"> from inline SVG markup.
function extractPath(svg: string): string {
  return /\sd="([^"]+)"/.exec(svg)?.[1] ?? "";
}
```
This regex grabs only the *first* `d="…"` match, silently dropping any `<circle>`/`<rect>`/`<line>`/additional `<path>` — which is exactly why multi-shape icons render broken in the current `IconPicker.vue`.

By contrast, pantoken's own icon token generation (`formats/icons/src/index.ts:59-68`, sourced from `@pantoken/tokens`'s vendored `raw.json`/IR built in `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` from the resolved `@instructure/ui-icons` package) carries the icon's full SVG markup as one opaque data-URI value straight from the upstream token IR — there's no per-shape regex extraction step in this path at all, so there's nothing to truncate.

### 3. Does VitePress already import the full `icons.css`? Yes — globally, already.

`docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts:24`:
```ts
import "../../../formats/components/generated/icons.css";
```
This is a *global* theme import (alongside `utilities.css` at line 23), loaded on every docs page already — not per-page.

Additionally, the paired pieces needed for the glyphs to actually render are also already global:
- The full `--instui-icon-*` value sheet is `docs/.vitepress/theme/generated/site-themes.css` (1,806,275 bytes, contains all 1,830 `--instui-icon-*` custom-property definitions), imported at `docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts:9`.
- The shared painter (`.instui-icon { display: inline-flex }` and `[class*="-icon-"]::before { ...mask: var(--pantoken-glyph)... }`) lives in `docs/.vitepress/theme/generated/components.css:1705-1717`, imported at `docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts:17`.

So the entire icon-glyph rendering stack — token values, glyph classes, and painter — is **already loaded on every docs page**, including the icon-picker page.

### 4. Feasibility for `IconPicker.vue` — trivially feasible, no new wiring needed

Since all three pieces (token sheet, `icons.css`, painter CSS) are already global theme imports, `IconPicker.vue` doesn't need any page-scoped import at all — it can render `<span class="instui-icon -icon-<name>" aria-hidden="true"></span>` immediately and it will just work, using CSS that's already shipped to every page. There's no bundle-size concern to solve for this specific approach since nothing new needs loading.

(For reference, precedent for page-scoped/dynamic loading does exist elsewhere in this docs site if it were ever needed: `IconPicker.vue:52` and `:66` use `defineAsyncComponent`/dynamic `import()` for lazy-loading the large manifest JSONs per tab, and `docs/.vitepress/config.ts:604` references a static `demos-assets/icons.css` asset path used for the standalone iframe demo runners outside the main theme.)

**Bottom line:** Switching `IconPicker.vue` to render via `.-icon-<name>` CSS glyph classes is both correct (full multi-shape SVGs, verified) and structurally simpler than fixing `docs/scripts/cdn-icon-manifest.ts`'s path-extraction regex — the CSS and custom properties needed are already globally loaded by `docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts`, so no new import or page-scoping work is required.</result>

### 6. Fix broken InstUI icon rendering — `docs/scripts/cdn-icon-manifest.ts` + `IconPicker.vue`

Root cause confirmed: `docs/scripts/cdn-icon-manifest.ts:14-16`'s `extractPath()` —

```ts
function extractPath(svg: string): string {
  return /\sd="([^"]+)"/.exec(svg)?.[1] ?? "";
}
```

— runs a non-global regex against the icon's full SVG markup and returns only the *first* `d="..."`
match anywhere in the string (used at line 26: `path: extractPath(icon.svg)`). Lucide icons routinely
compose a base shape (`<circle>`, `<rect>`, a triangle `<path>`) plus separate detail `<path>`/`<line>`
elements (a stem, a dot); `extractPath` keeps only one of them and silently drops the rest, or returns
`""` when the first/only shape element has no `d` attribute at all (e.g. a bare `<rect>`). Confirmed
against the generated manifest: `info` keeps only the vertical stem (circle outline and dot lost),
`square` and `circle-alert` come out as `path: ""` (nothing renders — those are `<rect>`/`<circle>` +
`<line>`s with zero `<path>` elements), `triangle-alert` keeps only the outline (stem + dot lost) —
exactly the "renders as a bare circle/triangle/square" symptom reported. The upstream data is not at
fault: `packages/core/src/icons.ts`'s `lucideModuleToSvg()` already reconstructs the full multi-element
`<svg>` correctly; the loss happens only in this docs-local extraction step.

Fix:
- In `docs/scripts/cdn-icon-manifest.ts`, replace `extractPath()` with an `extractInnerMarkup(svg)` that
  captures everything between the outer `<svg ...>` and `</svg>` tags (e.g.
  `/<svg[^>]*>([\s\S]*)<\/svg>/.exec(svg)?.[1] ?? ""`), and change the manifest field from `path` to
  `markup` (rename at the write site, line 26, and in the emitted JSON shape). Leave the existing
  `viewBox` extraction alone — it's a single-attribute regex and not lossy.
- In `IconPicker.vue`: rename `InstUiEntry.path` → `InstUiEntry.markup` (interface at lines 6-11), and
  change the render (lines 252-259) from a single `<path :d="icon.path" />` to
  `<svg class="icon-picker__svg" :viewBox="icon.viewBox" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" v-html="icon.markup"></svg>`.
  This is a deliberate `v-html` use — flagged here rather than silently introduced — but it's safe: the
  markup is fully build-time-generated from vetted source (`lucide-react`'s shipped module source and
  pantoken's own `custom` icon set, both parsed in `packages/core/src/icons.ts`), baked into a static
  JSON asset at build time, never runtime or user-supplied input. It's also the only approach that's
  correct for both `lucide` and `custom` sources regardless of how many shape elements an icon uses,
  without hand-rolling an SVG element parser.
- Re-run whatever generates `cdn-icon-manifest-instui.json` (part of the `docs:assets` script per
  `docs/package.json`) so the fix takes effect, and re-check the four icons named above render fully.

# Changesets

pantoken now uses Changesets for release metadata, version bumps, and changelog generation.

## Command map (vp task -> underlying command)

- `vp run changeset:add` -> `vpx changeset`
- `vpr release -p <pkg[@version|@alpha|@beta|@rc]> [-p <pkg[@...]> ...]` -> full local release cut (gates, deterministic `bumpp`, commit, tag, push)
- `vpr release <pkg[@version|@alpha|@beta|@rc]> [<pkg[@...]> ...]` -> same as above using positional package specs
- `vp run release:status` -> `vpx changeset status --verbose`
- `vp run release:version` -> `vpx changeset version`
- `vp run release:plan:package` -> build publish set from a package tag into `.release-plan.*`
- `vp run release:notes:package` -> generate `release-notes.md` from `.release-plan.json`
- `vp run release:changelog:root` -> regenerate root `CHANGELOG.md` in strict chronological order
- `vp run release:changelog:root:seed` -> one-time bootstrap mode to backfill root `CHANGELOG.md` with synthetic `v0.1.0` entries for packages that do not have package tags yet
- `vp run release:publish` -> `vpx changeset publish`
- `vp run release:pre:enter` -> `vpx changeset pre enter next`
- `vp run release:pre:exit` -> `vpx changeset pre exit`
- `vp run gate:repository` -> validates publishable package `repository.url` metadata for npm provenance
- `vp run gate:publint` -> `publint` across publishable workspaces
- `vp run gate:attw` -> `attw --pack --profile strict --no-emoji` across publishable workspaces

## Contributor workflow

1. After making a release-impacting change, run `vp run changeset:add`.
2. Select impacted packages and choose the correct bump level.
3. Commit the generated markdown file in `.changeset/` with your PR.

Use `vp run release:status` to inspect pending release state.

- Replace the CDN picker's fake button-styled tabs with the real `.instui-tabs` component, add a page title, and elevate the card to a primary surface with `-shadow-resting` instead of a secondary bordered one.

content.text:
PR is up: [thedannywahl/pantoken#75](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/75).

**What changed:**
- [CdnPickerPage.vue](docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CdnPickerPage.vue) — real `.instui-tabs` instead of button-styled fake tabs, plus a page title.
- [CdnPicker.vue](docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CdnPicker.vue) — card is now an elevated primary surface (`-shadow-resting`), search field uses `.instui-input-group` with a search glyph, copy button has a copy glyph.
- [IconPicker.vue](docs/.vitepress/theme/components/IconPicker.vue) — InstUI icons and Simple Icons now render together in one list with a text+rule divider (no more fake tabs); combined selections merge into one output URL/snippet; dark-mode invert now follows the site's `.dark` class instead of OS preference; icons render via the real `-icon-<name>` glyph classes.
- [cdn-icon-manifest.ts](docs/scripts/cdn-icon-manifest.ts) — dropped the buggy single-path SVG extraction that was the root cause of most InstUI icons rendering as bare circles/rects/triangles.

Four incremental commits plus a changeset, `vpr ready` passing (195 test files, 1191 tests, lint/type-check clean), and manual verification in the browser covering the scaffold, interactions, the merged icon output, and the dark-mode fix.

* since we now have an icons tab, the components tab doesn't need the tokens sheet radios (lean / full) it should only be lean.
* Base and Utilities should be included in the components list, and they should be the first two entries, and checked by default.
* All components doesn't need the (components.css) trail in its label.
* All components should be a multi-state checkbox (indeterminate) that checks/unchecks the component list - not that disables it, but when everything is checked the built url should be `components.css` and not ever individual combined import.
* Output radio toggles should instead be secondary tabs that toggle between `@import` and `<link>` snippets.
This is a solid, concrete set of refinements. Let me rework `CdnPicker.vue` and the `cdn.ts` strings to match.

Align the CDN picker docs page with InstUI patterns: real tabs, an elevated primary card, and a merged icon list with a labeled divider instead of fake tab buttons. Also fixes the Simple Icons dark-mode invert (was keyed off the OS `prefers-color-scheme` instead of the site's own theme toggle) and broken InstUI icon glyphs (most icons rendered as a bare circle/rect/triangle because the manifest generator kept only the first `<path>` in a multi-shape icon).

Also simplifies the components tab: drops the now-redundant token-sheet toggle (icons live on their own tab), folds base/utilities into the component list as checked-by-default entries, turns "All components" into a tri-state checkbox that selects/clears the list (collapsing the output to `components.css` only when everything is checked), and replaces the output format radios with secondary tabs.

Two gotchas for a generator:
- `register()`'s `only` option expands transitively through `NESTED_DEPS` (`src/index.ts:179-182`: `date-input` needs `calendar`; `date-time-input` needs `date-input`) — but `NESTED_DEPS` is **not exported**, so your manifest/picker logic must hardcode this dependency map itself (or you request the pantoken team export it).

## 2. Build outputs — yes, both ESM and IIFE exist

`renderers/web-components/package.json:20-26` exports map:
```
"exports": {
  ".": "./dist/index.mjs",
  "./i18n.json": "./src/i18n.json",
  "./components.css": "./dist/components.css",
  "./*.css": "./dist/*.css",
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
No `main`, `module`, or `unpkg` field. `type: "module"`.

Actual `dist/` output (`renderers/web-components/dist/`):
- `index.mjs` (68 KB) + `index.d.mts` — ESM, externalizes `@pantoken/components`/`@pantoken/icons` as bare imports (per comment in `renderers/web-components/scripts/build-iife.ts:1-6`).
- `web-components.iife.js` (2.5 MB unminified-source-equivalent /  ~2.4 MB, minified, exposes global `PantokenWebComponents`) — built by `scripts/build-iife.ts:9-38`, bundles `@pantoken/components` + `@pantoken/icons` in (`external: []` at line 32), so it's a true drop-in `<script src>` file.

Important: **the IIFE file is not in the `exports` map at all.** It's reachable on jsDelivr/unpkg only because those CDNs serve raw published file paths and ignore `exports` (this exact point is called out in `CdnPicker.vue:71`: "jsDelivr serves raw file paths (it ignores the package `exports` map)"). - Default: importing `@pantoken/web-components` (ESM) auto-registers **everything** — `register()` is called unconditionally at module load (`renderers/web-components/src/index.ts:453`: `register();`).

type ManifestComponent = { name: string; needsIcons: boolean };

  a.name.localeCompare(b.name),
);

// Localized labels from the active locale's themeConfig.cdnPicker, falling back to English defaults.
const { theme } = useData();
const t = computed<CdnPickerStrings>(() => ({
  ...CDN_PICKER_DEFAULTS,
  ...(theme.value as { cdnPicker?: Partial<CdnPickerStrings> }).cdnPicker,
}));

// Deep-linking: restore state from the URL hash on setup, then keep it in sync as the user picks.
function initialSelection(): Set<string> {
  const raw = readHashParam("c_sel");
  if (raw === "all") return new Set(components.map((c) => c.name));
  if (!raw) return new Set();
  const names = new Set(components.map((c) => c.name));
  return new Set(raw.split(",").filter((n) => names.has(n)));
}

const selected = ref<Set<string>>(initialSelection());
// Base and utilities are structural includes, not entries in the component manifest — on by default.
const includeBase = ref(readHashParam("c_base") !== "0");
const includeUtilities = ref(readHashParam("c_util") !== "0");
const format = ref(readHashParam("c_fmt") ?? "link");
const search = ref(readHashParam("c_q") ?? "");

watch(includeBase, (v) => writeHashParam("c_base", v ? "1" : "0", "1"));
watch(includeUtilities, (v) => writeHashParam("c_util", v ? "1" : "0", "1"));
watch(format, (v) => writeHashParam("c_fmt", v, "link"));
watch(search, (v) => writeHashParam("c_q", v, ""));

function toggle(name: string): void {
  const next = new Set(selected.value);
  if (next.has(name)) next.delete(name);
  else next.add(name);
  selected.value = next;
}

All done — [PR #75](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/75) is fully updated and pushed, `vpr ready` clean.

**This round's additions:**
- **Base/Utilities**: renamed to just "Base"/"Utilities", each with an info button opening a `context-view` popover with a short blurb (sourced from the components package's own JSDoc, not invented copy).

Along the way I hit and fixed a couple of real issues: a literal `</script>` inside template-literal strings (and even inside comments) breaking Vue's SFC parser, and a race where clicking "All icons" before the larger Simple Icons manifest finished loading would silently select zero Simple Icons.

`renderers/web-components/src/elements/alert.ts:1,54` doesn't hardcode any `var(--instui-*)` itself — it imports `alertCss` from `@pantoken/components` and inlines the *generated string* into the shadow DOM (`` `<style>...${alertCss(ctx.I)}</style>` ``). - 19 refs to its own `--instui-component-alert-*` namespace
- 1 ref to **another component's** token: `--instui-component-base-button-medium-height` (for close-button padding math)
- `--instui-elevation-above`, `--instui-spacing-space-xs`
- 4 icon glyphs: `--instui-icon-info`, `-circle-check`, `-triangle-alert`, `-circle-x`

## 3. Is the token sheet already chunked anywhere?

No. `formats/css/package.json:20-26` exports exactly four entries: `.`, `./inject`, `./style.css`, `./style.lean.css` (plus `package.json`) — no per-category or per-component token exports. `formats/css/dist/` and `formats/css/generated/` contain only `style.css`/`style.lean.css` (plus the JS `index.mjs`/`inject.mjs`). A repo-wide search for category-named CSS (`*color*.css`, `*spacing*.css`, `*typography*.css`, `*elevation*.css`) outside icons turns up nothing in `formats/css`.

By contrast, `@pantoken/components` (`formats/components/package.json` exports block) *is* already granular: `./base.css`, `./utilities.css`, `./component-icons.css`, `./*.css` (57 per-component files in `formats/components/dist/`), `./icons.css`, `./icons/*.css` (1,828 individual per-glyph files, avg. 744 bytes each — `formats/components/dist/icons/monitor-pause.css` is 661 bytes), and `./components.css` (the full 142,825-byte barrel). ## 4. Would splitting the token sheet by category actually help, given jsDelivr `/combine/`?

**Existing combine precedent:** `docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CdnPicker.vue:84-96` already builds `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css/dist/style.lean.css,{base.css},{utilities.css},{component-icons.css},{<name>.css...}` — i.e., it **already uses the lean, not full, token sheet**, combined with per-component pieces and a conditional `component-icons.css` add-on (line 91, gated by the per-component `needsIcons` manifest flag). `IconPicker.vue:178-189` goes even further, combining individual per-glyph files (`icons/<name>.css`) rather than the icon barrel.

# Export NESTED_DEPS, per-element IIFE builds, right-size the token sheet, fix two picker bugs

## Context

This continues the CDN-picker work on the `cdn-picker-instui-refactor` branch (PR #75, already merged
several rounds of InstUI-alignment changes). The current ask is four things:

1. Export `NESTED_DEPS` from `@pantoken/web-components` — it's currently private, forcing the docs
   picker to hardcode a duplicate copy.
2. Give `@pantoken/web-components`'s IIFE build the same per-item granularity `@pantoken/components`
   already has for icons (`dist/icons/<name>.css`) — i.e. `dist/<name>.iife.js` per custom element,
   so a consumer who only wants `<instui-alert>` isn't forced to load the whole 2.5 MB bundle.
3. Validate whether the picker's token-sheet dependency (currently the full `@pantoken/css` `style.css`
   for every element, regardless of selection) can shrink, and whether the sheet itself needs
   chunking.
4. Two picker bugs found during use: the Components tab's "All components" checkbox doesn't
   symmetrically restore Base/Utilities when re-checked, and toggling Base/Utilities by hand doesn't
   move "All components" into its indeterminate state; and the Web Components tab's "All elements +
   ES module" output is a bare URL instead of a real `import` statement.

Research (three read-only passes over `renderers/web-components/`, `formats/css/`, and
`formats/components/`) settled the two open technical questions before this plan could be written:

**Token sheet — no chunking needed, just stop over-fetching.** `formats/css/dist/style.css` is a single
flat `:root { ... }` block (no component-level CSS at all) — confirmed via `formats/css/src/index.ts`
and by counting selectors in the built file. 82.6% of its 1.4 MB (145 KB gzip) is the `--instui-icon-*`
glyph data-URIs; `style.lean.css` (257 KB / 22.5 KB gzip) drops exactly those and nothing else
(`formats/css/src/index.ts:5-10,36-46`). Everything left after removing icons (component/color/
primitive/spacing/etc. tokens, ~250 KB) is `var()`-chained across those categories (a component token
resolves through a semantic-color token through a primitive token), so a category-level split
(colors.css/spacing.css/...) couldn't be loaded independently without breaking resolution — there's
nothing left worth chunking once icons are excluded. **`CdnPicker.vue` already does the right thing**
(lean sheet + a per-component `needsIcons` flag from `docs/scripts/cdn-manifest.ts:17-22` that
conditionally adds `component-icons.css`); `WebComponentsPicker.vue` is the one component still
pointing at the full `style.css` unconditionally. Fix: mirror `CdnPicker.vue`'s pattern exactly.

**Per-element IIFE — feasible, but only if a real bug in `register()`'s icon wiring gets fixed first.**
`renderers/web-components/src/index.ts:20` statically imports `@pantoken/icons`' `resolve`, used as
`iconSvg`'s default parameter (line 130) and assigned unconditionally into every `register()` call's
`ctx.iconSvg` (line 439) — regardless of `options.only`. Since Rollup/Vite can't code-split `iife`/`umd`
output (confirmed: multi-entry `lib.entry` is rejected in that format, and `rollupOptions.input` with
shared chunks throws "UMD and IIFE output formats are not supported for code-splitting builds"), any
per-element build that goes through the shared `register()` — the only registration path today — would
statically retain that reachable `@pantoken/icons` → `@pantoken/tokens` reference and bundle the full
~2.5 MB (`web-components.iife.js`'s current size) into **every** one of the 30 files, ~75 MB total, for
elements that mostly never touch an icon at all. Grepping every element file for actual `ctx.iconSvg(...)`
calls (not the separate, CSS-only `-icon-<name>` glyph painting most components use) found exactly five
that need it: `calendar`, `date-input`, `drilldown`, `rating`, and `icon` itself (which renders an
arbitrary caller-supplied name, so it needs the full resolver). `icon-button` just slots in a consumer-
supplied `<instui-icon>` (`icon-button.ts:19-23`) — no dependency, `NESTED_DEPS` is already complete as
`{"date-input": ["calendar"], "date-time-input": ["date-input"]}`. So the fix is: make the icon resolver
**injectable** in the shared ctx-building code (defaulting to the real one, preserving `register()`'s
current behavior for every existing consumer — plain import, selective `only`, the big IIFE — with zero
behavior change), and have the **new** per-element build entries pass a no-op resolver for the 25
elements that never call it. This is additive, not a breaking change to `register()`'s public API.

## Changes

### 1. `renderers/web-components/src/index.ts` — export `NESTED_DEPS`, make icon resolution injectable

- Add `export` to the `NESTED_DEPS` const (currently lines 179-182) and move it next to `ELEMENTS`
  (after line 115), with a doc comment matching `ELEMENTS`'s style (lines 78-83) explaining it's the
  map `register()`'s `only` option expands through.
- Extract the ctx-building body of `register()` (lines 404-444: prefix/registry/onCommand/wrapper/
  locale/strings/firstDay setup, ending in the `ctx: RegisterContext = {...}` literal) into an internal
  helper, e.g. `buildRegisterContext(options, resolveIconSvg: (name: string) => string): RegisterContext`,
  parameterized on the icon resolver instead of hardcoding `iconSvg` at line 439.
  - `register()` keeps its exact current signature and default behavior: calls
    `buildRegisterContext(options, iconSvg)` (the real, `@pantoken/icons`-backed one) — no change for
    any existing consumer (plain import, selective `only`, the big IIFE all keep working identically).
  - `buildRegisterContext` and a tiny local no-op (`() => ""`) become available for the **build script**
    to import directly from source (this package's own build already compiles its own `src/`, so this
    isn't the cross-package raw-CSS-import problem the docs site hits) — they don't need to be published
    in `package.json`'s `exports` map, just present in `src/`.
- Add an exported (or internal, whichever reads cleaner alongside `ELEMENTS`) list of the five element
  names that actually call `ctx.iconSvg` — `["icon", "calendar", "date-input", "drilldown", "rating"]`,
  found by grepping every `src/elements/*.ts` for `iconSvg(` (already done during research; re-verify at
  implementation time in case an element changed). `date-time-input` doesn't call it directly but nests
  `date-input`/`calendar`, which do.

### 2. `renderers/web-components/scripts/build-iife.ts` — build one small IIFE per element

- Keep today's single call that builds `dist/web-components.iife.js` (the "everything" bundle, real
  icons, unchanged) — it's still needed for the picker's "select all" case and any existing consumer of
  that URL.
- Add a loop over `ELEMENTS` (imported from `../src/index.ts`) that runs a **separate** Vite `build()`
  call per element (multi-entry is not an option for `iife`/`umd`, per the research above), each with:
  - A synthetic entry (a small generated module, not 30 hand-authored files) that imports
    `buildRegisterContext` + that element's `DEFINITIONS` record and calls
    `def.define(buildRegisterContext({}, ICON_ELEMENTS.includes(name) ? iconSvg : noopIconSvg))`, wrapped
    so it self-registers on load exactly like today's big bundle does (auto-invoke at module scope,
    guarded by `typeof HTMLElement === "undefined"` the same way `register()` already is at the bottom
    of `src/index.ts`).
  - `fileName: () => \`${name}.iife.js\``, same `formats: ["iife"]` / `external: []` as the existing
    single build (per-element files fully bundle their deps too — there's no other way for a classic
    script tag).
  - Per-element files register **only their own element** — no nested-dep baking. `date-time-input`'s
    shadow markup renders `<instui-date-input>`, which renders `<instui-calendar>`, so a consumer needs
    all three tags defined; that's the picker's job to combine (below), the same way jsDelivr's
    `/combine/` already concatenates multiple small CSS files elsewhere in this picker suite — a
    concatenated `<script>` of multiple self-invoking IIFEs executes each in order in the same global
    scope, so as long as the combine URL lists dependencies first (calendar, then date-input, then
    date-time-input), each `customElements.define()` call sees its dependency already defined.
- Expected result: ~25 files stay small (a few KB — just that element's own definition + spacing/wrapper
  plumbing, no icon payload); `icon`/`calendar`/`date-input`/`drilldown`/`rating` stay large-ish (still
  bundle `@pantoken/icons`/`@pantoken/tokens`, unavoidable — they need real glyph data); `date-time-input`
  stays small itself (it doesn't call `iconSvg` directly) but always ships combined with its two
  icon-needing dependencies in practice.

### 3. `renderers/web-components/package.json` — expose the new files

- Add a wildcard subpath export mirroring `formats/components/package.json`'s `"./icons/*.css": "./dist/icons/*.css"`
  pattern: `"./*.iife.js": "./dist/*.iife.js"`.
- While touching this: the existing single `dist/web-components.iife.js` has **no** export entry today
  (it's reachable only via direct jsDelivr dist-path access, which ignores `exports` maps) — add
  `"./web-components.iife.js": "./dist/web-components.iife.js"` too, for consistency, since it costs
  nothing and doesn't change current CDN consumption.

### 4. `docs/.vitepress/theme/components/WebComponentsPicker.vue`

- **Token sheet**: replace the hardcoded full `style.css` reference with the same pattern as
  `CdnPicker.vue`'s `needsIconSheet` — compute whether any selected element is in the
  `ICON_ELEMENTS` list (hardcoded here too, same five names, same reasoning as `ELEMENTS`/`NESTED_DEPS`
  already hardcoded in this file per the existing comment about why source/dist import isn't viable).
  When none of the selected elements need icons, use `style.lean.css`; when any do, use
  `style.lean.css` + `component-icons.css` (matches `CdnPicker.vue`'s combine pattern) — never the full
  `style.css`. Update `tokenNote`'s copy accordingly.
- **ES module "all selected" fix**: `esmSnippet`'s `allSelected` branch currently returns the bare string
  `"https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components"` — change to the full statement
  `'import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";'`, matching the pattern already used for the
  non-"all" branch and for `IconPicker.vue`'s analogous all-selected case.
- **Classic script tag, per-element case**: when not everything is selected, build a jsDelivr combine
  URL of the specific selected elements' `dist/<name>.iife.js` files, expanded through `NESTED_DEPS` and
  **ordered so dependencies come first** (calendar, then date-input, then date-time-input — a simple
  explicit ordering is enough given the graph is two shallow chains, no general topo-sort needed). Feed
  that combine URL into the existing bootstrapper IIFE's injected `<script src>` (replacing the
  hardcoded big-bundle URL) alongside the now-conditional token `<link>`. When everything is selected,
  keep using the existing single `web-components.iife.js` URL (simpler, already correct, no combine
  needed).

### 5. `docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CdnPicker.vue` — fix the tri-state Base/Utilities interplay

Two bugs in the current `toggleAll`/`someSelected` logic:

```ts
function toggleAll(checked: boolean): void {
  selected.value = checked ? new Set(components.map((c) => c.name)) : new Set();
  includeBase.value = false;       // always false regardless of `checked` — wrong
  includeUtilities.value = false;  // same
}
const someSelected = computed(() => selected.value.size > 0 && !allSelected.value); // ignores base/util
```

Fix: treat "All components" as a true master over {every component, Base, Utilities} — checked only
when all three are on, indeterminate when it's a mix:

```ts
function toggleAll(checked: boolean): void {
  selected.value = checked ? new Set(components.map((c) => c.name)) : new Set();
  includeBase.value = checked;
  includeUtilities.value = checked;
}
const allComponentsSelected = computed(
  () => components.length > 0 && selected.value.size === components.length,
); // unchanged meaning, renamed — still drives combineUrl's components.css collapse, unaffected by base/util
const allSelected = computed(
  () => allComponentsSelected.value && includeBase.value && includeUtilities.value,
); // now the master checkbox's "fully checked" state
const someSelected = computed(
  () => !allSelected.value && (selected.value.size > 0 || includeBase.value || includeUtilities.value),
);
```

`combineUrl`'s barrel-collapse check (`if (allSelected.value) files.push(components.css)`) must switch
to `allComponentsSelected.value` — collapsing to the full component barrel is a name-based decision only,
independent of whether Base/Utilities happen to be on.

## Process

- Continue on the existing `cdn-picker-instui-refactor` branch (PR #75) — this is a direct continuation
  of that work, not a new feature branch.
- Commit incrementally: the `register()`/build-script/package.json changes in `renderers/web-components`
  as one or two commits, the docs picker changes as separate commit(s), consistent with this branch's
  existing history.
- Add a changeset for `@pantoken/web-components` (this is a real, publishable package change — a minor

   picker to hardcode a duplicate copy.
2. Give `@pantoken/web-components`'s IIFE build the same per-item granularity `@pantoken/components`
   already has for icons (`dist/icons/<name>.css`) — i.e. `dist/<name>.iife.js` per custom element,
   so a consumer who only wants `<instui-alert>` isn't forced to load the whole 2.5 MB bundle.
3. Validate whether the picker's token-sheet dependency (currently the full `@pantoken/css` `style.css`
   for every element, regardless of selection) can shrink, and whether the sheet itself needs
   chunking.
4. Two picker bugs found during use: the Components tab's "All components" checkbox doesn't
   symmetrically restore Base/Utilities when re-checked, and toggling Base/Utilities by hand doesn't
   move "All components" into its indeterminate state; and the Web Components tab's "All elements +
   ES module" output is a bare URL instead of a real `import` statement.

Research (three read-only passes over `renderers/web-components/`, `formats/css/`, and
`formats/components/`) settled the two open technical questions before this plan could be written:

flat `:root { ... }` block (no component-level CSS at all) — confirmed via `formats/css/src/index.ts`
and by counting selectors in the built file. 82.6% of its 1.4 MB (145 KB gzip) is the `--instui-icon-*`
glyph data-URIs; `style.lean.css` (257 KB / 22.5 KB gzip) drops exactly those and nothing else
(`formats/css/src/index.ts:5-10,36-46`). Everything left after removing icons (component/color/
primitive/spacing/etc. tokens, ~250 KB) is `var()`-chained across those categories (a component token
resolves through a semantic-color token through a primitive token), so a category-level split
(colors.css/spacing.css/...) couldn't be loaded independently without breaking resolution — there's
nothing left worth chunking once icons are excluded. **`CdnPicker.vue` already does the right thing**

shared chunks throws "UMD and IIFE output formats are not supported for code-splitting builds"), any

statically retain that reachable `@pantoken/icons` → `@pantoken/tokens` reference and bundle the full

- Add `export` to the `NESTED_DEPS` const (currently lines 179-182) and move it next to `ELEMENTS`
  (after line 115), with a doc comment matching `ELEMENTS`'s style (lines 78-83) explaining it's the
  map `register()`'s `only` option expands through.

  locale/strings/firstDay setup, ending in the `ctx: RegisterContext = {...}` literal) into an internal

  nothing and doesn't change current CDN consumption.

   "All components" should return to fully checked. Uncheck "All components" → Base and Utilities should

  needed).

### 5. `docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CdnPicker.vue` — fix the tri-state Base/Utilities interplay

Two bugs in the current `toggleAll`/`someSelected` logic:

```ts
function toggleAll(checked: boolean): void {
  selected.value = checked ? new Set(components.map((c) => c.name)) : new Set();
  includeBase.value = false;       // always false regardless of `checked` — wrong
  includeUtilities.value = false;  // same
}
const someSelected = computed(() => selected.value.size > 0 && !allSelected.value); // ignores base/util
```

Fix: treat "All components" as a true master over {every component, Base, Utilities} — checked only
when all three are on, indeterminate when it's a mix:

```ts
function toggleAll(checked: boolean): void {
  selected.value = checked ? new Set(components.map((c) => c.name)) : new Set();
  includeBase.value = checked;
  includeUtilities.value = checked;
}
const allComponentsSelected = computed(
  () => components.length > 0 && selected.value.size === components.length,
); // unchanged meaning, renamed — still drives combineUrl's components.css collapse, unaffected by base/util
const allSelected = computed(
  () => allComponentsSelected.value && includeBase.value && includeUtilities.value,
); // now the master checkbox's "fully checked" state
const someSelected = computed(
  () => !allSelected.value && (selected.value.size > 0 || includeBase.value || includeUtilities.value),
);
```

`combineUrl`'s barrel-collapse check (`if (allSelected.value) files.push(components.css)`) must switch
to `allComponentsSelected.value` — collapsing to the full component barrel is a name-based decision only,
independent of whether Base/Utilities happen to be on.

## Process

- Continue on the existing `cdn-picker-instui-refactor` branch (PR #75) — this is a direct continuation
  of that work, not a new feature branch.
- Commit incrementally: the `register()`/build-script/package.json changes in `renderers/web-components`
  as one or two commits, the docs picker changes as separate commit(s), consistent with this branch's
  existing history.
- Add a changeset for `@pantoken/web-components` (this is a real, publishable package change — a minor

/**
 * Static element metadata with no other dependencies — no CSS imports, no `@pantoken/icons`. Kept
 * separate from `../index.ts` specifically so build scripts (which run via plain Node, not through
 * this package's own Vite/esbuild pipeline) can import it directly without pulling in the raw `.css`
 * imports the element definitions transitively depend on, which plain Node can't load.
 *
 * @module
 */

/**
 * The base (unprefixed) element names this package registers. {@link register} mints a tag per name
 * under its `prefix` option — `icon` → `<instui-icon>` by default, or `<x-icon>` for `{ prefix: "x" }`.
 * A prefix is always applied (a custom-element name must contain a hyphen), so an empty or nullish prefix
 * falls back to the default `instui`.
 */
export const ELEMENTS = [
  "icon",
  "button",
  "alert",
  "badge",
  "pill",
  "tag",
  "avatar",
  "spinner",
  "progress",
  "metric",
  "rating",
  "progress-circle",
  "icon-button",
  "toggle-button",
  "truncate",
  "img",
  "side-nav-bar",
  "tree-browser",
  "calendar",
  "tooltip",
  "modal",
  "context-view",
  "popover",
  "tray",
  "in-place-edit",
  "drilldown",
  "pages",
  "drawer-layout",
  "date-input",
  "date-time-input",
] as const;

/**
 * Elements whose shadow markup renders another element, so registering one requires its dependencies
 * too: `<instui-date-time-input>` renders a `<instui-date-input>`, which renders a `<instui-calendar>`.
 * {@link register}'s `only` filter expands through this (transitively) so a cherry-picked subset still
 * works. Keyed by base name; values are direct dependencies.
 */
export const NESTED_DEPS: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>> = {
  "date-input": ["calendar"],
  "date-time-input": ["date-input"],
};

/**
 * Base element names that actually call {@link iconSvg} to render an inline glyph, as opposed to the
 * separate, CSS-only `-icon-<name>` glyph painting most components use (a mask on a CSS custom
 * property, no JS resolution involved). `date-time-input` isn't listed because it doesn't call
 * `iconSvg` itself — it nests `date-input`/`calendar` (see {@link NESTED_DEPS}), which do.
 */
export const ICON_ELEMENTS = ["icon", "calendar", "date-input", "drilldown", "rating"] as const;

<result>## Summary

VitePress's code-fence + copy-button system is split cleanly into two independently-reusable pieces: a **markdown-it plugin that emits a plain HTML string at build time** (no Vue/directive involvement), and a **single global delegated DOM click-listener** that the client app wires up once. The Shiki highlighting itself is 100% Node/build-time and isn't shipped to the browser at all. Below are the exact files/lines, followed by the reuse implications.

All paths resolve through the pnpm symlink `docs/node_modules/vitepress -> ../../node_modules/.pnpm/vitepress@2.0.0-alpha.19_.../node_modules/vitepress`. Everything under `dist/node` is bundled into one file, `dist/node/chunk-B0BRqWJx.js` — there's no separate `highlight.ts`/`.js` in `dist/`, it's inlined.

### 1. HTML structure — generated as a plain string, at build time

`.../vitepress/dist/node/chunk-B0BRqWJx.js:21221-21226` — `preWrapperPlugin(md, options)`:

```js
md.renderer.rules.fence = (...args) => {
  ...
  return `<div class="language-${lang}${active}"><button title="${tooltipText}" data-copied="${copiedText}" class="copy"></button><span class="lang">${label}</span>` + fence(...args) + "</div>";
};
```

This is a **markdown-it renderer-rule override that string-concatenates HTML** — it wraps whatever the base `fence` renderer (Shiki's `codeToHtml` output) produced. Nothing here is a Vue component, directive, or client-side hydration step. The final structure, in DOM order, is:

```html
<div class="language-js">
  <button title="Copy Code" data-copied="Copied" class="copy"></button>
  <span class="lang">js</span>
  <pre class="shiki ..."><code>...<span class="line">...</span>...</code></pre>
</div>
```

Sibling order matters — see §2.

### 2. The copy button's click handler — global delegated listener, DOM-agnostic

`.../vitepress/dist/client/app/composables/copyCode.js:4-39` — `useCopyCode()`:

```js
window.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
  const el = e.target;
  if (el.matches('div[class*="language-"] > button.copy')) {
    const parent = el.parentElement;
    const sibling = el.nextElementSibling?.nextElementSibling; // <pre> tag
    ...
    const clone = sibling.cloneNode(true);
    ...
    let text = clone.textContent || '';
    const lang = /language-(\w+)/.exec(parent.className)?.[1] || '';
    if (isShell(lang)) text = text.replace(/^ *(\$|>) /gm, '').trim();
    copyToClipboard(text).then(() => { el.classList.add('copied'); ...});
  }
});
```

Registered exactly once, for the app's lifetime, in `dist/client/app/index.js:6,45` — inside the root `VitePressApp` component's `setup()` (comment: `// setup global copy code handler`), alongside `useCodeGroups()`.

**This is a real `window`-level delegated listener using `Element.matches()`** — it has zero knowledge of how the matching DOM got there. It doesn't care whether the `<div class="language-*">` came from pre-rendered markdown HTML or was rendered at runtime by any Vue component. **Answer to your question (a): yes, it will fire correctly for a Vue-rendered structure**, provided the DOM shape matches exactly:

- Element clicked must satisfy `div[class*="language-"] > button.copy` (direct child, not just descendant).
- `parent.className` must contain `language-<lang>` (used only to special-case shell prompts).
- Critically: `el.nextElementSibling.nextElementSibling` must be the `<pre>` element — i.e., **the button must be followed by exactly one sibling before the `<pre>`** (the `<span class="lang">`, even if you don't need/want a visible label — you can render it empty/hidden but it must occupy that sibling slot, or the copy handler will grab the wrong node or `undefined`).
- `copyToClipboard` (same file, lines 42-77) does `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, falling back to a `document.execCommand('copy')` textarea hack — same behavior as your current bespoke button, no VitePress-specific state needed.
- Visual feedback (`.copied` class, tooltip swap) is handled purely via CSS (`data-copied` attribute + `::before` content), not JS — see §4.

### 3. Shiki highlighting — Node-only, not reusable client-side without adding a new dependency

`.../vitepress/dist/node/chunk-B0BRqWJx.js:21544-21677` — `async function highlight(theme, options, logger)` calls `createHighlighter(...)` (imported from `shiki`, confirmed via `grep -n "shiki\|createHighlighter" chunk-B0BRqWJx.js:29-30`) and `highlighter.codeToHtml(str, {...})`. This whole function is `async`, uses dynamic `highlighter.loadLanguage(...)`, and is invoked from the markdown-it config pipeline during the Node build — it's never bundled into `dist/client`:

```
grep -rl "shiki" dist/client → only dist/client/theme-default/styles/components/vp-code.css
```

That CSS file (`.shiki span { color: var(--shiki-light/dark, inherit) }`) is pure CSS reading inline custom-properties Shiki injects per `<span>` — no JS. So Shiki's runtime footprint on the client is **zero**; it's exclusively a devDependency-side, build-time tool.

Confirmed in `vitepress`'s own `package.json`: `shiki@^4.4.1`, `@shikijs/core`, `@shikijs/transformers`, `@shikijs/types` are all under vitepress's **regular `dependencies`**, and none appear anywhere in `dist/client`. In this repo's own manifests, `docs/package.json` has no `shiki`/`@shikijs/*` entry at all (only `vitepress: catalog:` at `docs/package.json:59`); `pnpm-lock.yaml` shows `shiki@4.4.1` and the `@shikijs/*` family only as **transitive** entries pulled in by vitepress itself (lines ~4736-4780, ~8257, ~11176+), not as a direct project dependency.

**Answer to (b):** Using Shiki client-side for the dynamic snippet would be a genuinely new client-bundle addition, not "free" — you'd need to add `shiki`/`@shikijs/*` directly to `docs/package.json` and call `createHighlighter`/`codeToHtml` yourself in the Vue component (Shiki does support browser/WASM usage, but it's still extra weight: the oniguruma/JS regex engine plus per-language grammar JSON, easily tens to a couple hundred KB depending on how many languages/themes you load and whether you use the WASM or pure-JS engine, fetched async). It is *not* pulled in "free" by vitepress's own client build, because vitepress's client only needs the CSS variables Shiki already baked into the pre-rendered HTML at build time — it never re-highlights in the browser.

### 4. Precedent and existing CSS in this docs site

- `docs/.vitepress/theme/pantoken.css:26-59` already targets **native** VitePress fences directly by selector — `div[class*="language-"]:has(+ .css-example)` and `.vp-doc div[class*="language-"]:has(+ .css-example)` — to seam code fences into `.css-example` preview frames used on CSS-API pages (`docs/.vitepress/config.ts:614-624`, the `liveExample` markdown-it hook). This confirms native `.language-*` fences are already used and styled elsewhere in this exact theme, and that theme CSS piggybacks on VitePress's default `.vp-doc [class*='language-']` rules rather than reimplementing them.
- No existing Vue component in `docs/.vitepress/theme/` renders a runtime `.language-*`/`button.copy` structure — `PickerOutput.vue` (`docs/.vitepress/theme/components/PickerOutput.vue:55-64`) is the only dynamic code-block component, and it's fully bespoke (`.picker-output__code`, `.picker-output__copy` using InstUI button classes, plain `<pre><code>{{ output }}</code></pre>`, own `navigator.clipboard.writeText` in `copy()` at lines 24-32).
- `PickerOutput.vue` is only ever used inside `CdnPicker.vue`, `IconPicker.vue`, `WebComponentsPicker.vue` (`grep` for `PickerOutput` import), which are embedded in normal markdown docs pages (e.g. `docs/guide/cdn-picker.md`). Those pages render through the theme's `Layout.vue` (`docs/.vitepress/theme/Layout.vue:1-9`), which is a thin wrapper (slots only) around VitePress's default `Layout` — so the default theme's `VPDoc.vue` still supplies the `.vp-doc` wrapper class (`node_modules/.pnpm/.../vitepress/dist/client/theme-default/components/VPDoc.vue:46`). **This matters**: nearly all of the native code-fence CSS is scoped under `.vp-doc` (e.g. `.vp-doc [class*='language-'] > button.copy` at `vp-doc.css:491`), so a runtime-rendered block inside `PickerOutput.vue` on a normal doc page will already sit inside `.vp-doc` and pick up the full default styling automatically, with no extra CSS work.
- Full relevant style block: `node_modules/.pnpm/.../vitepress/dist/client/theme-default/styles/components/vp-doc.css:338-583` — covers the outer `div[class*='language-']` container, `pre`/`code` padding and tab-size, `button.copy` (idle opacity 0, hover/focus opacity 1, `.copied` state swapping in `--vp-icon-copied` and a `content: attr(data-copied)` tooltip pseudo-element), and `span.lang` (absolute-positioned language label, fades out on hover so the copy button tooltip has room). These are all pure CSS variables (`--vp-code-copy-code-bg`, `--vp-code-lang-color`, etc.) — no JS wiring beyond the click listener in §2.

### Direct answers

**(a) Can you reuse VitePress's real copy-button handler as-is?** Yes. It's a single `window`-level delegated `click` listener (`copyCode.js:7`) registered once for the whole SPA lifetime by the root app (`app/index.js:45`), matched purely by CSS selector (`div[class*="language-"] > button.copy`) and DOM sibling-position (`button.nextElementSibling.nextElementSibling` → `<pre>`). It has no awareness of build-time vs. runtime origin. To use it, your Vue component's render output must exactly match markdown-it's emitted shape: `<div class="language-xxx"><button class="copy" title="…" data-copied="…"></button><span class="lang">xxx</span><pre><code>…</code></pre></div>` — same tag types, same sibling order (the `span.lang` slot is load-bearing for the sibling-walk even if you hide it), rendered inside a `.vp-doc`-ancestor page so the CSS applies.

**(b) Is client-side Shiki realistically wireable?** Yes it's technically possible (Shiki ships a browser/WASM build), but it's a real new dependency you'd add to `docs/package.json` — not something already riding along in the client bundle. Budget for grammar/theme JSON payload and async `createHighlighter()`/`loadLanguage()` calls; it's comparable in shape to adding a lightweight syntax highlighter, not "turning on a switch."

**(c) Minimal faithful approach:** Reuse the DOM shape from `preWrapperPlugin` (§1) and the `.vp-doc` CSS (§4) as-is — that gets you pixel-identical styling and the working native copy button (§2) for free, with zero new dependencies. <script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, watch } from "vue";

const props = defineProps<{
  formats: { value: string; label: string }[];
  modelValue: string;
  output: string;
  hasSelection: boolean;
  emptyText: string;
  formatLabel: string;
  copyText: string;
  copiedText: string;
}>();
defineEmits<{ (e: "update:modelValue", value: string): void }>();

const copied = ref(false);
// A copied snippet goes stale the moment the underlying selection changes — revert the button
// immediately instead of waiting out the confirmation timeout.
watch(
  () => props.output,
  () => (copied.value = false),
);

async function copy(): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await navigator.clipboard.writeText(props.output);
    copied.value = true;
    setTimeout(() => (copied.value = false), 1500);
  } catch {
    // Clipboard blocked — the code stays selectable in the block.
  }
}
</script>

5	 * dropping the output into `.vitepress/theme/custom.css` (alongside `@pantoken/css`, which defines
6	 * the custom properties) re-skins the docs with the Instructure look while light/dark keeps flowing
7	 * through the same tokens.
8	 *
9	 * @module
10	 * @beta
11	 */
12	
13	import { VITEPRESS_VARS_CSS } from "./vitepress-vars.ts";
14	
15	/** Options for `toVitePressCss`. */
16	export interface ToVitePressCssOptions {
17	  /** The selector the variables are emitted under (default `":root"`). */
18	  selector?: string;
19	}
20	
21	/**
22	 * Emit the VitePress → Instructure CSS-variable bridge.
23	 *
24	 * Wraps the variable mappings in the specified selector (default `:root`).
25	 *
26	 * @internal
27	 * @param options - {@link ToVitePressCssOptions}.
28	 * @returns The bridging CSS string wrapped in the selector.
29	 */
30	export function toVitePressCss(options: ToVitePressCssOptions = {}): string {
31	  const selector = options.selector ?? ":root";
32	
33	  // If using default selector, return the CSS as-is from the source file.
34	  // Otherwise, extract variables and re-wrap in the custom selector.
35	  if (selector === ":root") {
36	    return VITEPRESS_VARS_CSS;
37	  }
38	
39	  // For custom selectors, extract the declarations from :root and wrap them
40	  const declarations = VITEPRESS_VARS_CSS.split("\n")
41	    .filter((line) => {
42	      const trimmed = line.trim();
43	      return trimmed.startsWith("--vp-") && trimmed.includes(":");
44	    })
45	    .map((line) => line.trim());
46	
47	  return `${selector} {\n  ${declarations.join("\n  ")}\n}\n`;
48	}

1	# CDN & distribution
2	
3	pantoken publishes every package to npm, so you can pull tokens, components, and web components straight
4	from a CDN — no build step, no bundler. This page covers the CSS combine URL (with an interactive
5	builder), plus the web-component drop-ins.
6	
7	## The token foundation
8	
9	Every pantoken component reads `--instui-*` custom properties from a token sheet on the page. Two
10	variants ship:
11	
12	- `@pantoken/css/dist/style.lean.css` — the recommended CDN foundation. It carries every token except the
13	  full icon set, so it's about 23 KB gzipped.
14	- `@pantoken/css/dist/style.css` — the full sheet, including all ~1,777 icon glyph tokens
15	  (`--instui-icon-*`). About 140 KB gzipped. Load this if you reference icons broadly via
16	  `var(--instui-icon-*)`.
17	
18	The elevation scale and focus-ring variables ride in both sheets, so shadows and the focus ring work with
19	just the foundation loaded.
20	
21	## Pick your components and icons
22	
23	The [interactive CDN picker](/guide/cdn-picker) builds jsDelivr combine URLs for both components and icons. Open it, check what you need, and copy the generated `<link>` or `@import` tag.
24	
25	- **Components tab** — choose individual component stylesheets or the whole `components.css` barrel. Add the base reset or spacing/color utilities if you need them.
26	- **Icons tab** — choose individual icons from the InstUI set (~1,800 icons) or from Simple Icons (~3,300 brand glyphs). The picker outputs a separate combine URL for the icon CSS files so you can load only the icons you actually use.
27	
28	Each component file is small — most are around 2 KB. A component that renders icons (`alert`, `checkbox`,
29	and a few others) needs those glyphs, so the builder adds `@pantoken/components/dist/component-icons.css` (about
30	0.5 KB gzipped — the 11 icons the component set uses) whenever you pick the lean sheet. The full sheet
31	already carries them.
32	
33	### Load order and fonts
34	
35	Load the token foundation first, then the optional base reset, then the component files. The combine URL
36	above already orders them for you. Fonts are the one exception: `@pantoken/components/dist/fonts.css` points at
37	font files by relative path, so combine can't rewrite them — load it as its own `<link>`:
38	
39	```html
40	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/components/dist/fonts.css" />
41	```
42	
43	### Everything at once
44	
45	Check **All components** in the picker to switch it to the barrel, or point at it yourself (about 141 KB
46	gzipped) alongside the token sheet:
47	
48	```html
49	<link
50	  rel="stylesheet"
51	  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css/dist/style.css,npm/@pantoken/components/dist/components.css"
52	/>
53	```
54	
55	## Web components
56	
57	`@pantoken/web-components` registers framework-agnostic `<instui-*>` custom elements. They inline their
58	own CSS, but still read tokens from a sheet on the page, so load a token foundation too.
59	
60	### ES modules (recommended)
61	
62	An ESM CDN resolves the package's dependencies for you. This registers every element:
63	
64	```html
65	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/dist/style.css" />
66	<script type="module">
67	  import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
68	</script>
69	```
70	
71	Use the full token sheet (or the lean sheet plus `component-icons.css`) so icon-rendering elements like
72	`<instui-alert>` resolve their glyphs.
73	
74	To register just some elements — and their nested dependencies — import `register` and pass `only`:
75	
76	```html
77	<script type="module">
78	  import { register } from "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
79	  // Pulls in date-input and calendar automatically.
80	  register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] });
81	</script>
82	```
83	
84	### A classic script tag
85	
86	For a no-modules drop-in, load the IIFE build. It bundles its dependencies and auto-registers every
87	element on load, exposing a `PantokenWebComponents` global:
88	
89	```html
90	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/dist/style.css" />
91	<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/web-components/dist/web-components.iife.js"></script>
92	```
93	
94	It's larger than the ESM path — it inlines `@pantoken/components` and `@pantoken/icons` — so reach for it
95	only when you can't use modules.
96	
97	## Pinning versions
98	
99	The URLs above — and the ones the picker writes — track the latest release. Pin a major (or exact)
100	version for production — for example `@pantoken/css@0` — so an upgrade never surprises you.
101	
102	## What's not here
103	
104	There's no `?components=button,badge` query parameter: no public CDN assembles a bundle from query params.
105	The combine URL is the closest equivalent, and the picker writes it for you.
106
